title: Dizziness and Low Blood Pressure in Parkinson's
content: People with Parkinson's disease can sometimes experience dizziness, lightheadedness or faintness, particularly when standing up. One possible cause is orthostatic hypotension, which is a drop in blood pressure after moving from lying or sitting to standing. Symptoms may include dizziness, weakness, blurred vision, feeling faint, or actual fainting. Parkinson's itself, dehydration, certain medications and other medical conditions can contribute to low blood pressure. Dizziness has many possible causes and should not automatically be attributed to Parkinson's disease. Persistent, recurrent or worsening dizziness should be discussed with a healthcare professional, especially if it involves fainting, falls or other new symptoms.
